page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.4xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the ecs.se1ne family, running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU hardware accelerators, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance tradeoff between single-core and multi-core operations. The instance exhibits weak single-core performance, as demonstrated by a Geekbench single-core score of 893.0 and a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1108.98, both falling into the bottom 10% to 25% categories. Conversely, multi-core execution scales to average levels, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 5757.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 13025.11. Memory bandwidth remains stable at average levels, measuring 75.3 GB/sec for large block read-only operations, though the overall Passmark memory score is weak at 1805.89.

Given its 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the ecs.se1ne.4xlarge offers a memory-optimized resource density suitable for workloads that require substantial memory capacity without demanding high single-threaded CPU performance. It achieves average throughput in database operations, static web serving, and multi-threaded decompression. However, it is poorly suited for single-threaded compression tasks or heavy computational workloads that cannot be parallelized. This profile makes it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for memory-intensive applications such as caching layers, database hosting, and moderate multi-threaded processing.
